data.gender_notes: Nuraan is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Nur' meaning light. Named for those who bring light and positivity to others. The name Nuraan carries the meaning “Light” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Nuraan usually hope their child will grow to embody light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who are a guiding light in the lives of others.
data.etymology: Nuraan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nuraan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nuraan is widely used and popular among Muslims, particularly in regions with a high Muslim population such as South Asia and the Middle East. The name holds a deep significance as the bearer of this name is believed to be a source of positivity, guidance, and light for those around them. The Cultural impact of this name extends to the naming of children, honoring ancestors, and serving as a reminder of the virtues that can be cultivated in a person.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Nuraan is considered a blessing and a reminder to serve as a beacon of light and positivity in the world. It is a call to embody the qualities of patience, kindness, humility, and forgiveness. The name is believed to have a protective virtue, shielding the bearer from harm and ensuring a ‘light’ and joy-filled life. Nuraan is also a connection to the divine Creator, whose infinite light illuminates the world and guides us all towards our true purpose.
